command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
since=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "round" && $4 !~ /^fix-specs#/ { print $1; exit }')
start=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "task" && $4 == "started" { print $1; exit }')
[ -n "$since" ] || since=$(git rev-parse "$start^" 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
review="$reports/review-specs.md"
hunks=$(git diff -U0 "$since" -- "$review" | grep -E '^[-+]' | grep -vE '^(---|\+\+\+) ' || true)
removed=$(printf '%s\n' "$hunks" | grep -E '^-' | grep -vxF -- '-- Status: open' || true)
added=$(printf '%s\n' "$hunks" | grep -E '^\+' | grep -vE '^\+(- Status: |- Resolution: |  +[^ ])' || true)
[ -z "$removed$added" ] || { printf '%s\n' "$removed" "$added" | grep .; echo "only the '- Status:' lines and the new '- Resolution:' lines (continuation lines indented) of $review may change - restore the rest with: git checkout $since -- $review, then re-apply the statuses"; exit 1; }

findings.message: The R1/R2 revisions misstate how the reused owner behaves while city data loads. specs/meeting-share-dialog/spec.md:10 (reference line) says the device zone's exemplar city falls back to "the zone id while the city data loads", and spec.md:58 (Share language choice) says the device time location's line falls back to "the stored label, then the zone id, while the city data loads". design.md D6 (line 113) likewise says the DEVICE_TIME label falls back "to the stored label and then the zone id, as presentLocationRows already does on screen". The owner they cite, useExemplarCity (packages/client/src/controller/useExemplarCity.ts:29-35), returns `(loadedSearch ?? readLoadedCitySearch(load))?.getExemplarCity(timeZoneId, cityNameLanguage) ?? deriveCityNameFromTimeZoneId(timeZoneId)`. That is a city name derived from the zone id (Asia/Almaty -> "Almaty"), never the zone id or the stored label, and it is undefined only for an undefined zone. presentLocationRows.ts:71 (`context.deviceTimeCityLabel ?? location.timeZoneId`) reaches the zone id only in that undefined case. As written, the normative spec text describes loading behaviour the owner does not have and would enter openspec/specs on archive, or push the implementer to fork or alter the owner (.claude/rules/glossary.md: "If the owner does not fit the need, change the owner and its tests"; no decision or task does that). Fix: in both spec sentences and in D6, state the real fallback (the name derived from the zone id while the city data loads), or add a decision and a task that changes useExemplarCity.
